status_semantics.status: All tickets are proposed, not started.
status_semantics.readiness: ready means no listed blockers; blocked means prerequisite tickets must be completed or reconciled as already satisfied.
status_semantics.optional: Optional tickets never block required delivery tickets; all external actions need the applicable execution authorization.

default_execution_rules: Reconcile existing work before creating an issue or editing code; use current code and issue state, not this snapshot alone.
Work the ready dependency frontier in isolated worktrees with fresh implementer context and pinned spec/ticket pointers; use topological_order rather than numeric ticket order.
Use behavior tests with independently checked expected results; avoid private-method tests and self-generated truth.
Preserve public URLs, immutable released identities, raw source bundles and explicit uncertainty.
Use expand-migrate-contract for schema-wide changes; retain a rollback-compatible previous publication.
Local PostgreSQL with required lexical search and optional pgvector ranking plus DuckDB/Parquet support research/processing; the hosted site remains static Astro with no required database or model.
Optional local Gemma, an HCK/ACQ executor adapter and RuleSpec export do not gate required delivery; pin verified current interfaces if an optional experiment is selected.

Relevant public/already-authorized source discovery, acquisition/refetch and schema backfills are authorized; prefer official bulk/API paths, preserve raw-version provenance and license/reuse basis, and respect per-source limits without repeated confirmation for ordinary in-scope collection.

tickets.title: Reconcile the merged plan with current code and work already tracked
tickets.delivers: An implementer can identify which proposed capabilities are already complete, partial, absent or superseded and select a genuine ready task.
acceptance_criteria: Pin the tracker/data/related-source commits examined and inventory existing issues, PRs, schemas, workflows and published data identities.

Inventory each new schema field against available and missing source evidence, including metadata, temporal endpoints and assertions; map gaps to relevant public/already-authorized sources and an acquisition or explicit-unknown disposition.
Map every backlog item to existing work or an explicit new gap; retain completed capabilities and document superseded recommendations.

Record local PostgreSQL with required lexical retrieval, optional pgvector ranking, DuckDB/Parquet, optional local Gemma, and static Astro; an HCK/ACQ executor adapter and RuleSpec export remain optional.
Publish a reviewable decision register and dependency graph without creating external issues or changing repository policy.
tickets.independent_validation: A second reviewer samples existing-code, existing-issue and new-gap mappings against the pinned sources; detect any recommendation that contradicts current behavior.
tickets.demo: Walk from an existing implemented feature and a confirmed gap to their disposition and next ready ticket.
tickets.rollback_notes: Revise the plan records; no product state changes.
tickets.implementation_notes: Use the current Matt Pocock to-spec/to-tickets methods; do not run an installation or restart already settled interviews. Relevant source discovery and acquisition to resolve these gaps are already authorized under the backlog data-acquisition policy; do not restrict the schema to current repository payloads.

tickets.title: Protect published release identities from replacement
tickets.delivers: A bookmarked or pinned release always resolves to the same published content.
acceptance_criteria: Remove force replacement of published release tags/identities; an existing identity with different bytes produces an explicit collision failure.

Existing public links remain resolvable and a promotion log records the correction relationship.

tickets.title: Preserve complete release catalogs and paginate API fallbacks
tickets.delivers: A reader and importer can find every cataloged release and detect incomplete API fallback history rather than silently accepting the first response page.
acceptance_criteria: A proposed synthetic fixture of 103 distinct release identities retains all 103 in the complete catalog, history navigation and import selection; this fixture is not a claim about live corpus totals.

The current static manifest path remains the primary historical source. The GitHub tag fallback must paginate beyond its observed per_page=100 request, and file-history fallback must paginate beyond its observed per_page=50 request or explicitly declare a bounded/incomplete scope.
Pagination ends only on verified exhaustion; duplicate pages, a failed later page or a resource cap produce explicit completeness results rather than silent truncation.
The eight-item commit preview stays a presentation choice; it must not define the underlying catalog/history completeness.
tickets.independent_validation: Create an independently enumerated synthetic 103-release fixture and a 53-commit history fixture. Check exact identity sets, navigation beyond the first pages, duplicate-page behavior and failure of the final page.
tickets.demo: Navigate to synthetic release 101 and commit 51, then inspect the incomplete state when the next API page fails.
evidence_to_close: Synthetic fixture provenance and expected identity sets
tickets.rollback_notes: Restore the preceding validated catalog artifact or disable the fallback with an explicit unavailable state; do not silently treat a first page as complete.
tickets.implementation_notes: Observed at the pinned tracker snapshot: DiffViewer reads static manifest pairs first; its fallback fetches tags with per_page=100 without a pagination loop. getFileHistory requests commits with per_page=50. No 60-release cap was verified. Counts 103 and 53 are proposed synthetic regression cases, not observed production counts.

tickets.title: Scale historical backfill with complete scope accounting and bounded resources
tickets.delivers: An operator can process the intended corpus and history in batches with a truthful completeness report and controlled storage/compute use.
acceptance_criteria: Enumerate the intended source/title/release scope from verified catalogs rather than hardcoded page/display caps.

Run resumable batches with bounded concurrency, memory, disk and retry budgets; record failures per scope.
Measure artifact growth, ingest cost and query/export performance before setting production defaults; use Parquet/DuckDB reports to verify accounting.

Claim completeness only for an enumerated declared scope whose required partitions are all accepted. Exclusions and unavailable data remain visible and narrow the coverage claim; they cannot satisfy a missing required partition or be counted as successful completion.

Keep acquisition/processing completeness separate from semantic certainty: a fully processed source scope can contain explicit unknown, conditional or disputed legal facts, but unavailable required partitions cannot count as complete.

tickets.title: Query publication, actual knowledge and evidence-backed applicability separately
tickets.delivers: A researcher can ask a bounded historical question in an explicit temporal mode and see a qualified answer with its source evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Expose three explicit modes for one representative provision family: as-published by immutable release identity, known-as-of by the tracker’s actual recorded observation/acceptance time, and applicability-on by a requested legal date and any declared necessary facts.

A late backfill of an old publication does not fabricate earlier tracker knowledge. If actual historical observation evidence is unavailable, known-as-of returns an explicit unknown/incomplete result.

Return evidence-backed applicability as known, conditional, disputed or unknown, preserving conditions, competing readings and evidence; never substitute release date for effective/applicability date.

Represent each temporal endpoint with an explicit known, open, unknown or conditional state, its date precision, basis and source evidence. An absent/null date means neither an open endpoint nor ongoing validity; use open only where the evidence supports that state and retain the limits of that evidence.
The CLI/query output and one static evidence panel expose the chosen mode, source/version identities, relevant dates, status and supporting spans without introducing a general legal decision engine.
tickets.independent_validation: Use an independently authored fixture with delayed effectiveness, retroactive applicability, a late backfill and conflicting applicability evidence. Fix expected answers for each mode/date before running the implementation; verify the same publication can differ between publication and actual knowledge timelines. Include known endpoints with differing precision, an evidence-supported open endpoint, an unknown/null endpoint and a conditional trigger; verify null never becomes a claim of continuing validity.
tickets.demo: Ask the same two-version provision question in all three modes, then backfill an older source and show that its earlier known-as-of answer remains unknown.
tickets.rollback_notes: Disable the new applicability projection or restore its prior accepted version; retain raw publication/observation history and return unknown where evidence is insufficient.
tickets.implementation_notes: Scope this to one representative provision family and a small fixture. Mode selection and evidence-status semantics are required; a universal historical-law solver is outside this ticket. Endpoint state and overall applicability result are separate: endpoint states are known/open/unknown/conditional; applicability results remain known/conditional/disputed/unknown. Acquire relevant missing public/already-authorized source evidence where available, otherwise preserve explicit uncertainty.

tickets.title: Reject stale local task attempts before accepting their artifacts
tickets.delivers: An operator can retry or supersede a local processing job without an older worker later publishing stale output over the new accepted generation.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a minimal local TaskAttempt lifecycle with stable task identity, input generation, attempt identity, lease, monotonically advancing fencing token and explicit terminal outcome.

Accept/promote an artifact only through an atomic compare-and-swap check against the current generation, required input identities and valid attempt/fencing ownership; expired or superseded attempts cannot win.
An identical accepted retry is idempotent; a changed input generation creates a new candidate and invalidates prior acceptance authority without rewriting immutable prior artifacts.
Expose attempt state and rejection reason through the existing local job/report interface; ordinary local execution remains available without a distributed scheduler or orchestration service.
tickets.independent_validation: Use a controlled two-worker fixture: worker A stalls, its lease/generation is superseded, worker B accepts the new generation, then A completes. Assert independently that only B’s artifact is current. Also exercise duplicate acceptance, lease expiry and interruption before/after the atomic acceptance commit.
tickets.demo: Run one small rebuild twice with a deliberate stale worker; show the new generation accepted, the old attempt fenced out and a duplicate retry safely treated as a no-op.
tickets.rollback_notes: Stop affected attempts, retain the last accepted immutable artifact and resume with a fresh generation/fencing token; do not recover by allowing stale workers to promote.
tickets.implementation_notes: This is a small local acceptance invariant used by USCT-019, not a distributed scheduler, queue platform or generalized workflow framework. Existing catalog/transaction facilities may supply the atomic compare-and-swap.

scheduling_semantics.dependency_rule: A ticket becomes eligible only when all its listed blockers are completed or reconciled as satisfied.
scheduling_semantics.ready_order: Among eligible tickets, prioritize earlier milestone, then stable ticket ID. This chooses a suggested presentation/pick order, not extra blocking edges.
scheduling_semantics.parallelism: Any independent eligible required tickets may run in parallel; priority order is not a serialization requirement.
scheduling_semantics.optional_work: Optional tickets are excluded from required_topological_order. Their position in the combined topological_order is illustrative eligibility only and never delays required milestones or cutover. Start one only when its optional experiment is selected.
scheduling_semantics.early_repair: USCT-033 is an M0 repair and therefore appears before M1 tasks once its existing blockers are satisfied, despite its later stable ID.
scheduling_semantics.cutover_gate: Every required ticket other than USCT-030 itself is a dependency ancestor of USCT-030; no optional ticket is a required ancestor.

dependency_validation.ordering_policy: milestone priority, then stable ticket ID among currently ready nodes

data_acquisition_policy.authorization: Relevant source discovery, acquisition/refetch and cross-source backfills needed for the new schemas are authorized for public sources and sources the user is already authorized to access. Do not request repeated confirmation for ordinary in-scope collection.
data_acquisition_policy.purpose: Fill evidenced schema-field and coverage gaps, including newly introduced metadata, temporal endpoints and assertion/evidence fields; collection is not restricted to data already in the repository.
data_acquisition_policy.source_preference: Prefer official bulk downloads and documented APIs; use other relevant public/authorized sources with their authority and evidence role explicitly labeled.
data_acquisition_policy.preservation: Preserve immutable raw source versions, retrieval/source identities, hashes, observation times, provenance and license/reuse basis; a refetch does not overwrite the prior raw version.
data_acquisition_policy.limits: Respect per-source rate, access, retention/reuse and request limits; checkpoint resumable work and report unavailable or incomplete scopes explicitly.
data_acquisition_policy.scope_limit: This authorization does not add permission for paid services, new restricted-account access or broad deployment. This artifact revision updates the plan and does not start production implementation.
